Valorizo a disponibilidade, cópias de segurança testadas e documentação simples. Gosto de apoiar equipas clínicas e de trabalhar com fornecedores para resolver problemas de desempenho. Sou metódico e calmo em situações de pressão, e prefiro processos simples e testados a soluções complicadas.

bullets: Giro 45 instâncias SQL Server com grupos de disponibilidade Always On.
Reduzi o tempo de restauro de 6 horas para 90 minutos com cópias diferenciais e testes mensais.
Otimizei consultas críticas do sistema de urgências, melhorando o tempo de resposta em 50%.
Automatizei tarefas de manutenção com PowerShell.
Defini políticas de acesso e auditoria alinhadas com o RGPD.
Apoiei utilizadores e criei pacotes SSIS para integração de dados.
Elaborei relatórios em SSRS.
Migrei bases de dados de servidores antigos para versões suportadas, sem perda de dados.
Dei formação a utilizadores avançados sobre consultas em T-SQL.
Participei em projetos de integração de dados entre serviços municipais e plataformas nacionais.
Prestei apoio técnico a utilizadores e instalei software.
Aprendi administração básica de bases de dados.
Documentei procedimentos de cópias de segurança.
Dei apoio de segunda linha a aplicações internas e resolvi bloqueios em bases de dados.
Escrevi manuais de utilização para equipas administrativas.

name: Bartosz Gniewek
headline: Database Administrator
summary: Database administrator with eight years of experience in MySQL and SQL Server for a regional retailer. I look after backups, user access and reporting databases. My day is mostly tickets, maintenance windows and tuning slow queries. I am keen to broaden my knowledge, and I keep up with industry trends by reading and attending internal talks. I prefer stable systems and clear documentation, and I enjoy helping colleagues understand what the database is doing.

bullets: Maintain 30 MySQL and SQL Server databases supporting stores and the web shop.
Schedule and verify nightly backups; ran a successful full restore test every quarter.
Tuned reporting queries, reducing a slow sales report from 15 minutes to 2.
Our developers use Kubernetes, Terraform and CI/CD tooling, and I attended an internal overview session but do not operate them.
Document database procedures and train new colleagues on backup and permission policies.
Handled user requests and permission changes.
Wrote T-SQL maintenance scripts.
Migrated small databases to new servers during planned weekend windows.
Created reports for the support team about slow queries.
Worked with the store systems team to plan upgrades before the holiday sales period.
Installed and configured workstations and printers for small businesses.
Resolved user tickets and kept an inventory of hardware.
Learned SQL basics from a senior colleague.
Supported a small team of developers by creating test copies of production databases.
Documented hardware and licence inventories for audits.

name: Eoin Calloran
headline: Senior Embedded Software Engineer
summary: Firmware engineer with twelve years of experience in medical and industrial devices. I write safety-conscious C, bring up new boards and debug at the register level. Prefer simple designs that can be certified. I enjoy mentoring and have a strong interest in verification and test automation for firmware. I enjoy simple, reviewable designs and careful documentation, including everything an auditor will ask for.

bullets: Developed infusion pump firmware in C on Cortex-M4 under IEC 62304 class C processes, and documented every residual risk with the quality team ahead of the notified body audit.
Wrote a secure bootloader with signed firmware updates over UART.
Cut standby current from 180 µA to 35 µA through sleep mode tuning.
Mentor two junior engineers and review all driver code.
Introduced automated unit tests and static analysis, reducing defects found in system test by 35%.
Implemented Modbus and CAN stacks for industrial drives.
Created hardware-in-the-loop test rigs.
Developed a bench test framework in Python that cut regression testing from two days to four hours.
Collaborated with regulatory staff to support product audits.
Developed Modbus communication modules that are still deployed in customer plants.
Wrote driver code for sensors and displays in C.
Learned schematic reading and debugging with oscilloscopes.
Supported production testing of a new product line.
Contributed to a safety review and implemented fixes for findings in the driver code.
Created test scripts to validate sensor accuracy on the production line.

name: Mateus Figueiredo Sarmento
headline: Engenheiro de Firmware
summary: Engenheiro de firmware com cinco anos de experiência em dispositivos IoT alimentados a bateria. Desenvolvo drivers, comunicações sem fios e atualizações remotas. Gosto de medir o consumo antes de otimizar. Gosto de trabalhar com equipas de hardware e de aprender com problemas reais de campo. Escrevo código claro, meço consumo antes de otimizar e gosto de testar em hardware real, não apenas em simulação.

bullets: Desenvolvi firmware em Zephyr para sensores de qualidade da água com autonomia de três anos.
Implementei atualizações OTA seguras sobre BLE e LoRaWAN.
Criei ferramentas de teste em Python que validam a leitura de sensores em bancada.
Reduzi o consumo médio em 30% ajustando temporizadores e modos de suspensão.
Colaborei com a equipa de hardware na escolha de componentes e na revisão de esquemas.
Programei microcontroladores STM32 para quadros de controlo.
Apoiei a integração com protocolo Modbus.
Reduzi o tempo de arranque de um quadro de controlo em 40%.
Documentei interfaces e escrevi testes de integração.
Coordenei com fornecedores de módulos de comunicação e validei amostras antes da produção.
Montei protótipos e programei placas Arduino para recolha de dados.
Aprendi a usar osciloscópios e analisadores lógicos.
Escrevi relatórios técnicos de cada experiência.
Participei em testes de campo com sensores instalados em ribeiras e cursos de água.
Escrevi relatórios de teste e listas de problemas conhecidos para a equipa.

name: Nkechi Umeadi
headline: Embedded Systems Engineer
summary: Embedded engineer working on solar-powered metering and monitoring devices for off-grid communities. Four years in the field; I enjoy robust, low-power designs that survive heat, dust and unreliable networks. I am a hands-on problem solver who is not afraid of travelling to remote sites to diagnose devices. I enjoy working with limited hardware, patchy networks and practical constraints, and I document what I learn for the next engineer.

bullets: Wrote firmware for prepaid solar meters with GSM connectivity and local fallback when the network drops.
Added watchdog and brown-out handling that cut field resets by 80%.
Collaborated with hardware engineers on board revisions and field failure analysis.
Documented a repeatable flashing and test procedure for the factory.
Train field technicians to install and troubleshoot meters, and write simple guides in English and Igbo.
Assisted with prototype testing and soldering.
Logged sensor data with Arduino based loggers.
Wrote firmware for a temperature logger used in a cold storage pilot.
Presented a final project that won a departmental prize.
Validated new component suppliers by building small test fixtures and comparing failure rates.
Built a prototype energy monitor for a final year project.
Tested sensors and calibrated readings against a reference meter.
Wrote the thesis and presented results to a panel.
Helped build a solar charge controller prototype and tested it outdoors in various weather conditions.
Wrote weekly lab reports summarising test results.

name: Jürgen Falkenrath
headline: Principal Embedded Engineer
summary: Embedded engineer with twenty years in automotive electronics, now a technical lead for body control and diagnostics software. I work with AUTOSAR, functional safety and a lot of paperwork. Terse communicator, thorough reviewer. I prefer clear requirements, careful reviews and well documented interfaces. I mentor newcomers in the importance of traceability and clean interfaces, and I like solving stubborn timing problems.

bullets: Lead six engineers delivering ASIL B body control software for two vehicle platforms, and kept every requirement linked to a design element and a test case for the assessors.
Implemented UDS diagnostic services and flash bootloader for ECUs, which has been used successfully in several series production vehicles since launch.
Introduced static analysis and MISRA checking; cut review findings by 40%, and checked the results against defined coding rules before every release.
Coordinate with suppliers and the test team on release planning and defect triage.
Present safety and software milestones to customers and external assessors.
Developed CAN and LIN drivers for door modules.
Supported validation on test benches.
Developed diagnostic routines used by service garages worldwide.
Reduced build times by 50% by restructuring the software configuration.
Supported production start with the supplier, including flash tooling and end-of-line checks.
Programmed 8-bit controllers in assembly and C.
Learned automotive protocols and tooling from senior colleagues.
